system.summary: Marked numerical groups represent French words and word parts.

diacritics.note: Superscripts and trailing strokes distinguish numerical groups in the strict transcriptions.

prior_solution.where: Period decipherments in Nationaal Archief, 2.01.08 inv. 248. No. 23 trained the table. The two March test references were sealed separately. Before fitting, the investigator had seen a small view of scan 174 including part of a French page. The January investigator had seen its clear copy.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed this project. AI agents transcribed the documents and performed the tests.

solution.what: Revisited my 14 November inventory survey (my own working notes, made with AI agents, not in this repository), identified period decipherments and separated the Vienna papers from the Düsseldorf target.
Two readers transcribed each cipher panel independently before reconciliation. The French references were transcribed separately.
January within-letter test matched two of five predictions, both de. Of 1,000 shuffled controls, 226 tied or exceeded that score. The investigator had seen the French reference.
Two monotone dynamic-programming alignments against the period copy for No. 23 agreed on 93 marked group candidates, 53 whole words and 40 fragments.
The frozen table predicted 43 whole tokens for No. 26. 32 matched the sealed French source within the registered position window. Best shuffled score 16.
The same table predicted 61 tokens for No. 21. 48 matched the sealed source within the registered window. Best shuffled score 20. The sole complete word assembled from fragments missed.
In the separate Düsseldorf comparison only two word placements were testable, below the minimum of eight. The unread companion was left untested.
Independent readings of the later inventory 204A annotations placed the reported 227 in a Munich dispatch. None of the notes entered the Vienna fit.

validation.notes: This contribution has sparse, position-tolerant word predictions and no continuous token-aligned reading for an n-gram test. The frozen March protocols compare the fixed table against two historical decipherments and 1,000 shuffled tables per letter.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The March table was fitted to No. 23 and its contemporary decipherment in the same archive file.

credits.note: Partial reconstruction and two prospective cross-letter tests of the marked numerical table, with AI agents. All four historical readings predate this work.
French clear copies used for training and comparison.

outcome.notes: The selected predictions use a positional tolerance and count words against historical references. They supply no document-wide read share. Three whole-word candidates matched every opportunity across both held-out letters. Most of the 93 entries remain provisional.
